chunks: Aban narrated from Zurarah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the slaves of the People of the Covenant, I used to buy something from them, so he said: 'Buy from them if they acknowledge slavery for them.'

key_terms.أَهْلِ ٱلذِّمَّةِ: People of the Covenant (non-Muslims living under Muslim rule)

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for buying slaves from the People of the Covenant in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) specifies that purchasing slaves from the People of the Covenant (Ahl al-Dhimmah) is valid only when they explicitly acknowledge their status of slavery, ensuring the transaction is based on their recognized condition. This ruling highlights the importance of clear consent and established legal status in Islamic commercial jurisprudence, particularly regarding non-Muslim subjects under Islamic rule. The condition prevents ambiguity in ownership and aligns with the broader Shia principle of fairness in trade transactions.
